-i: Sets the target IP/hostname to connect WinRM to
-p: Sets the login password — appears as plaintext in the command, watch for it leaking via logs/shell history
-s: Sets an attacker-side script folder that can be uploaded/run on the target — opens a real code-execution path on the target
-e: Sets an attacker-side executable folder ready to upload and run on the target — high risk, equivalent to delivering a payload onto the machine
-S: Uses SSL/TLS for the WinRM connection (usually paired with port 5986)
-P: Sets the port to connect to (default 5985, or 5986 for SSL)
-l: Enables logging of the session's connections/commands
--no-colors: Disables color in the session output
